chapter: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
title: His Memphis birthplace on Mississippi Boulevard
summary: Jones recalls the address area of the house where he was born and the porch swing hooks still there.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Jimmy, I was going back over the first three reels and I ran across a remark of yours where you said that you could remember the address of the house where you were born, or you could remember the house where you were born. Do you remember the address?
It was -- let's see, 10 something. I can't remember the last two numbers. But it was on Mississippi Boulevard in Memphis.
That's an interesting piece of history to have.

Yeah, and one of the things I really remembered when I went back with my father, they used to have like little swings on the porch, and the hooks were still on the porch where the swings used to hang down when I was an infant. You know?
And I said, gee whiz, they must be a hundred years old or something, you know?
No -- well, okay. But it was just nice to know, and they tell me that the house is still standing there and people are still living in it, you know?
